MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 24, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on August 24, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on August 19, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Closed Session for the City Council; the City council Sitting as the Governing Board of
  the Mission Viejo Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency; the city
  Council in its capacity as the Legislative Body of the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Finance Authority, as Potential Plaintiffs Conference with Legal Counsel-
  Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9: (Two Cases).

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-
  Price and Terms
City Council Minutes  1  August 24, 2021
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Outlined her concerns about the agenda process that took place on the
  Stein Mart property negotiations. Stated that the whole process was unethical.

CS3. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Cunningham, Roth: Agency
  Claimed Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant
  to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (2 cases).

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced one case under CS1. the City Council unanimously voted to
participate in the lawsuit that the Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) has brought
against the State regarding the extraordinarily high affordable housing requirements. The belief is
that the State miscalculated. In all of the other matters, the City Council was advised and gave
direction but nothing to be reported occurred.

Mayor Kelley announced she would like to move item 28 up to be discussed after the Consent
Calendar. By consensus the City Council concurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander on her Retirement

  Presented proclamation to Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander.

P2. School Spotlight - Newhart Middle School

  Received presentation from Principal Judith Murphine.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke on the Voter’s Rights Act and history of Hispanic candidates that ran
for City Council. Stated her reasons there was a Brown Act Violation.

Aaron Hand, M.V.: Voiced his concerns of the lack of transparency by the City and the City
Council regarding the apparent manipulation of the lawsuit against the City regarding at-large and
district-based elections. Questioned the Council terms.

CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  2  August 24, 2021
 Items 13 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
remainder of the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of July 13, 2021, as presented.

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated July 9, 2021 in the Amount of $1,982,593.41

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated July 16, 2021 in the Amount of $1,244,600.86

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated July 23, 2021 in the Amount of $587,669.82

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated July 30, 2021 in the Amount of $2,076,862.29

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated August 6, 2021 in the Amount of $862,393.61

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2021

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for June 2021

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  August 24, 2021
 10. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for June 2021

  Received and filed.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2021

  Received and filed.

12. Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending June 30, 2021

  Received and file the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending June
  30, 2021.

14. 2020 Residential Resurfacing - Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 21838) -
  Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

15. Rubberized Surfacing Replacement - Florence Joyner Olympiad Park: Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City.

16. Age Well Senior Services Contract for Senior Mobility Program

  Approved Age Well Senior Services Agreement (A21-42) for Services with the Senior
  Mobility Program.

17. 2021 Residential Resurfacing - Slurry Seal (CIP 22838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal,
  Inc.(A21-43) in the amount of $858,137.50.

18. Refund Request for Permit 146155 in the amount of $20,066.75

  Authorize the City Manager to approve refund request for Permit 146155 in the amount of
  $20,066.75.
City Council Minutes  4  August 24, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28. Resolution Expressing Support for the Establishment of a Veterans’ Cemetery in the
  County of Orange, City of Anaheim, California

  Mayor Kelley presented her report.

  The following spoke in favor: Wayne Yost, Dana Point; Bill Cook, M.V.; and John Carson,
  M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 21-31 Reaffirming the Support of the City Council for Bringing a Veterans'
  Cemetery to the County of Orange in the City of Anaheim.

  Council Member Sachs asked if Council Member Goodell would rescind his second to allow
  Council Member Raths, a retired Coronel to second the motion. Council Member Goodell
  rescinded his second.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt Resolution 21-
  31 Reaffirming the Support of the City Council for Bringing a Veterans' Cemetery to the
  County of Orange in the City of Anaheim.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

13.  MV Shuttle Contract Amendment

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell to
  approve the Second Amendment with LAZ Parking California, Inc. for the operation of the
  MV Shuttle.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

19. Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on Parcels Less than One Acre for the

City Council Minutes  5  August 24, 2021

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

20. Agreement with ClientFirst Consulting Group, LLC for EnerGov Land Management
  System Implementation Assistance

  Acting Director of Information Technology David Meyer presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
  agreement with ClientFirst Consulting Group, LLC (A21-44) and issued purchase orders in
  amounts not to exceed $137,400 for implementation assistance, business process refinement,
  and data conversion services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

21. Information Technology Strategic Plan

  ClientFirst Consultants David Krout and Tom Jakobsen presented the report.

  Council Members asked various questions and by consensus received the report.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

22. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2021 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  Mayor Kelley appointed herself as voting delegate and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum as alternate
  for the League of California Cities Conference Annual Business Meeting on Friday September
  24, 2021.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum to approve
  these appointments.

City Council Minutes  6  August 24, 2021
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths,
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

23. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Kelley.

24. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

25. Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

No report was given.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

26.  Overview of he Voting District Formation Process

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed concerns over the timeline for the District Voting process
  particularly that the map process will be during the holiday season. She stated that the
  process once again will benefit the incumbents.

  City Attorney Bill Curley responded that map Z was repeatedly stated as being an example
  not a map for consideration. He stated that his power point is the Fair Map Act. Elections
  Code 21600-21640 is exactly what is in the power point.

  Cathy Kadison, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of Walt Lawson questioning the District process
  timeline and how citizens can get involved.

  By consensus the City Council received the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

27. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  7  August 24, 2021
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell started off by congratulating the four Nadadore swimmers that
represented the United States in the Olympics. Annie Lazor earned a bronze medal in the 200-meter
breast stroke and Zach Apple earned two gold medals for the 4 by 100 free style relay and the 4 by
100 medley relay. Michael Benninger got a lot of great experience competing in the 800 and 1500-
meter freestyle and Haley Anderson came in tenth place in the 10,000-meter open water swim. He
also announced the Mission Viejo Dive Team won the National Championship this past month.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the City Attorney for all his hard work explaining the process for
district voting. Also, thanked the IT department for their presentation this evening. He stated he
attended the Pacific Symphony and thanked staff for their amazing job. Council Member
complimented on the improvements of the landscape at the Mission Viejo Post Office.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs pointed out to the public that Secure O.C. Schools is preparing a semi-
annual report. The vigilance that is necessary now more than ever, which became evident in New
Mexico when a thirteen-year-old killed a classmate this past month. He expressed concerns with
the horrific psychological effects on kids on school children. He asked that the school districts
reach out to the SRO’s in looking for additional help in looking for clues that might indicate
attention that may be necessary to be managed. Since January this year there have been 27 school
shootings. Council Member Sachs noted the City lost a terrific General Manager at the Oso Creek
Golf Course due to the harassment of a few people who felt that they were more important than
anyone else that plays golf. The General Manager took it to heart and tried to please everyone and
she was ultimately driven away. He stated he was very disappointed and sad that Natalie was
leaving.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked Council Member Sachs from acknowledging the General
Manager’s departure from the golf course. She commented that it is very hard to find good workers
because a lot of people would rather sit home and not work. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum indicated
that she would like to honor our Nadadore Olympians at a future meeting. She asked for prayers
for American citizens and Christians that are being killed for their beliefs in Afghanistan at this
time and also holding up our brave soldiers in your prayers. She encourages parents to go to the
school board regarding mask mandates and stated that parents know what’s best for their children
not the government. She attended a golf team event in July at the Oso Creek Golf Course and in
August she attended the recognition of Harvey Ohman who is a long time Elks Member and The
Voice of the Diablos for over thirty years. She stated he is recognized all over the State for his
unique announcing of football games. He was inducted into the Mission Viejo High School
Football Hall of Fame along with Mark Sanchez. Mayor Pro Tem that she also attended he Pacific
Symphony and had a wonderful time and loved the theme, the doves, the butterfly them and thanked
city staff and all the volunteers. Lastly, she closed with a remembrance of Jon Petke.

Mayor Kelley

City Council Minutes  8  August 24, 2021
 Mayor Kelley announced that Trabuco Hills High School March Band will be in the Macy’s Day
Parade in New York City this year. They are fund raising and looking for local support where
checks can be made to Trabuco Hills High School Music Boosters and mail your check to City Hall
attention to Assistant City Clerk Renata Winter. Donors will be recognized in the Tournament of
Hills Program. Mayor Kelley mentioned that she visited the classroom of Dan Moreno ASB and
STEM Teacher of Los Alisos Middle School. She stated she also attended the Pacific Symphony
with her grandchildren. Thanked City Staff for this event. She stated the school is back in session
and hoping things go well for the school year. Lastly, she wishes Director of Technology Jackie
Alexander for her years of services to our city and appreciate her service.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:29 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Jon Petke, to Tuesday, September 14, 2021, at
5:00 p.m.

.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 14, 2021

City Council Minutes  9  August 24, 2021
